title: Integral generators of $D^b_c(X,E)$ and $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$
statement:
Let $X$ be a standing scheme and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite. Let $\mathcal G_E$ be the class of
objects $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]=E_X\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$, where
$a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is a locally closed immersion and $L_0$ a lisse finite free
$\cO_{E,S}$-module (locally on $S$), and $\mathcal G_{\Qlb}$ the class of
$\QbarX\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ for all finite $E$ and such $a$, $L_0$.

1. Every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained from $\mathcal G_E$ by finitely many cones and shifts.
2. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is obtained from $\mathcal G_{\Qlb}$ by finitely many cones and
   shifts (with one finite $E$ for the given object).
3. $a_!L_0\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and its reductions $a_!L_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cO_E/\pi_E^n=a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$
   lie in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$ and come from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$.

proof.text: Preliminaries for the locally closed extensions used below. A standing scheme is separated of finite type over the field in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]; the field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal, and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes X locally Noetherian. Finite type gives a finite affine cover, hence X is Noetherian. Open subschemes and closed subschemes have affine charts given by localizations and quotient rings, so the same holds for all the locally closed subschemes used here. The Noetherian topology and constructibility facts in [def-weil-constructible-subset] show that these schemes are qcqs, their open immersions are quasi-compact, and their locally closed strata are constructible. For a locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u$, use $a_!=i_*u_!$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], both factors are exact for any sheaf of coefficient rings. Their coefficient restrictions are the required ones by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. For locally closed $b:T\hookrightarrow S$, exactness, factorization independence and the canonical isomorphism $a_!b_!\simeq(ab)_!$ are precisely the statement of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence], applied with $R=\Lambda_X$. Its coefficients agree with ours by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The composite immersion is locally closed: write $S$ closed in an open $V\subset X$, and $T$ closed in an open $W\subset S$; lift $W$ to an open $V\prime\subset V$. Then $T$ is closed in $V\prime$ because the two affine quotient maps compose, and $V\prime$ is open in $X$.

source.place: (1): exactness and transitivity of locally closed extension by zero

proof.text:
For any lisse finite free integral module $M_0$ on a locally closed $b:T\hookrightarrow X$, apply [det-lem-integral-models-operations] (4) to $L=M_0$ and $M=E_X$, viewed as an integral module. The coefficient restriction is $b^*E_X=E_T$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], $E_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ is flat, and the same holds on $T$. Therefore this projection formula reads, in degree zero,
$$E_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}b_!M_0\simeq b_!(E_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}M_0)=b_!(M_0[1/\ell]).$$
Here exactness of $b_!$ is step 1, so its application to the degree-zero tensor calculation introduces no higher cohomology. This establishes the scalar-extension identity needed for every integral generator, without presuming any unproved commutation with an infinite colimit.

Let $K\in D^b_c(X,E)$. By [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation], it suffices to build each sheaf $a_!L$, with $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ locally closed and $L$ lisse, from integral generators. Apply [sk-lem-stratified-lattice] to the standing scheme $S$ and $L$. It gives a finite locally closed stratification carrying lisse finite free lattices $L_{0,b}$ in $L|_{S_b}$. Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] (1) to refine and order it so that the successive unions are open in $S$. On a refined stratum restrict the old lattice: a trivialization of a finite free module restricts to a trivialization, and its scalar extension still equals the restricted $L$, since inverse image is exact and monoidal. This uses the coefficient and exact-inverse-image identification of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]; lisseness after restriction is also [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] (2). Thus the refinement retains the lattices.

source.place: (1): generation, stratified lattices, and ordering the strata

proof.text: The lisse sheaf $L$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], using its finite free local models and the single stratum $S$. Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration] on $S$ to $L$ and the ordered stratification of step 3. It gives finitely many short exact sequences with quotients $b_!(L|_{S_b})$. Push these sequences forward by the exact $a_!$ of step 1; transitivity identifies their quotients with $(ab)_!(L|_{S_b})$. By step 2 and $L|_{S_b}=L_{0,b}[1/\ell]$, each is $( (ab)_!L_{0,b})[1/\ell]\in\mathcal G_E$. By [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], each short exact sequence of module sheaves gives a distinguished triangle of their degree-zero complexes in the ambient derived category. Induct on the filtration length: the zero first term is the rank-zero generator, and a triangle with earlier term and quotient already constructed expresses the next term as a cone up to a shift. This builds $a_!L$ by finitely many cones and shifts. Substitute these finite constructions into the finite cone construction of $K$ from [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation]; there are only finitely many such substitutions, proving (1).

source.place: (1): filtration, exact pushforward, and conversion of extensions to cones

proof.text:
For $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ choose one finite $E$ and $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ with $K\simeq(K_E)_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ by [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-objects]. The functor $T=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}-$ is exact: it is right exact as the extension-of-scalars left adjoint in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], and preserves finite limits by [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]. Since $T$ is exact, the derived extension $T_{E,\Qlb}=L(T)$ used in [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-objects] is the termwise functor $D(T)$, by the clause on exact functors in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Hence [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] shows that it preserves the cones and shifts in the construction of (1) for $K_E$. Its value on a generator is
$$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}(E_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}a_!L_0)\simeq \overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}a_!L_0.$$
This is the associativity of the relative tensor product: the maps on local pure tensors are $q\otimes(e\otimes m)\mapsto qe\otimes m$ and $q\otimes m\mapsto q\otimes(1\otimes m)$, mutually inverse and compatible with all balancing relations and restrictions. Thus all generators use this same $E$, proving (2).

source.place: (2): finite descent followed by exact scalar extension

proof.text: For (3), a lisse finite free $L_0$ on $S$ has finite constant local models $\mathcal O_{E,S}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_E^r$. This is precisely condition (1) of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], with the single stratum $S$; the rank may vary between trivializing opens. Hence the complex concentrated in degree zero is in $D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_E)$ by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Apply [det-lem-integral-models-operations] (3) to get $a_!L_0\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. This uses the blueprint's intrinsic category of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology; the integral criterion is an equivalent characterization, not an extra condition that must be proved anew here.

Fix $n\ge1$ and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. By [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] (1), $\mathcal O_{E,X}/\pi_E^n=(A_n)_X$, and likewise on $S$. Apply [det-lem-integral-models-operations] (4) with $L=L_0$ and $M=(A_n)_X$; its restriction to $S$ is $(A_n)_S$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Finite free modules are flat, and this is local on the trivializing cover, so $L_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}(A_n)_S=L_0/\pi_E^n$. The degree-zero formula and exactness from step 1 give
$$(a_!L_0)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_n)_X\simeq a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n).$$
The elementary flatness calculation here is that tensoring with $\mathcal O_{E,S}^r$ takes an exact sequence to its $r$-fold direct sum, so no higher terms of a flat resolution contribute. In particular the formula is derived reduction, not a claim that quotienting is exact on arbitrary integral sheaves.

On $S$, $L_0/\pi_E^n$ is locally the constant finite free $A_n$-module $A_n^r$. On $\overline S\setminus S$ and $X\setminus\overline S$ the sheaf $a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$ restricts to zero, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. These three locally closed pieces form a finite constructible stratification (discard empty pieces). Thus this degree-zero sheaf is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], so is in $D^b_c(X,A_n)$ by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. The coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] (4) states that $A_n$ is finite for $n\ge1$. With its quotient topology it is discrete; every ideal is a finite set and is generated by that set, so $A_n$ is Noetherian. Also $X$ is qcqs by step 1. Consequently [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical] applies to this very stratification: its restrictions are locally constant of finite type, and therefore the sheaf is classical, i.e. is a pullback from $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. This proves the remaining assertions of (3), with the cohomology of every reduction concentrated in the single interval $[0,0]$.
